summary: The Helmut-Schmidt-Programme is a DAAD scholarship scheme, funded by the German Federal Foreign Office, for future leaders from developing and emerging countries who want to take a master's degree in public policy and good governance. It supports seven selected English-taught master's courses at five German universities, starting in September or October 2027. Applicants apply directly to one or two of the courses; the DAAD and the courses select together. Studies are tuition-free and are funded by a monthly rate plus further allowances.
eligibility_notes:
You must be a graduate (bachelor or equivalent) with a well-qualified first university degree completed with above-average grades (upper third), in social and political sciences, law, economics, public policy or administration. You must want to contribute to the social, political and economic development of your home country or region. Both young graduates and mid-career professionals can apply, but you need practical experience relevant to the programme: work, internships, political or social commitment, volunteering, or work for charities or NGOs. The amount required differs by course.

Country and residence: you must live in a developing or emerging country on the DAAD list of countries (which follows the OECD DAC list of ODA recipients). Anyone who has spent more than the last 15 months in a country not on that list at the application deadline (31 July) is not eligible. You may already be in Germany if you have lived there for less than 15 months at the deadline. Eligibility depends on residence, not strictly on passport.

Degree timing: your last university degree must not be more than six years old (issued no earlier than 1 January 2020 for the 2027 round). Someone who will only graduate after the deadline cannot apply in this round; a person who has finished but has no certificate yet can give a confirmation from the university. There is no age limit.

If you already hold a master's degree you must explain well why you should be funded for another postgraduate degree and how it builds on the first.

Language: applicants do not need German, because the courses are taught in English. German courses in Germany before the studies are a mandatory part of the scholarship. The English level and certificate depend on each course (see the course entries).

Each course also sets its own selection criteria (degree, grades, language, experience), which you must meet in addition to the DAAD criteria. Courses: Social Protection asks for a bachelor's degree in economics/business administration, politics, law, administration, health, education, social science, psychology, international relations/development or related fields, good English, a written entry exam and at least five months of professional experience. Development and Governance asks for a four-year bachelor's degree in political science, social science, law or related, a strong record, very good English and at least one year of full-time professional experience at application. Public Policy asks for above-average grades, excellent English and at least one year of relevant professional experience. Peace and Conflict Studies asks for a bachelor's degree of 180 ECTS with at least 30 ECTS in social science, English at C1, good grades and at least three months of relevant work or study experience abroad. Management in Nonprofit Organisations asks for a bachelor's degree in politics, law, economics or administration, English at B2 and at least two years of non-profit experience plus volunteer work. Development Studies and Governance and Public Policy (both Passau) ask for upper-third grades, 60 ECTS in social sciences and/or economics (law also for the second), 10 ECTS of research methods, very good English and at least four months of professional or practical experience or social or political engagement.
age_experience_notes: No age limit. Relevant practical experience is an essential requirement (professional experience, internships, political or social commitment, volunteering or work for charities or NGOs). Minimum experience set by the courses: Social Protection five months; Development and Governance one year full-time at application; Public Policy one year; Peace and Conflict Studies three months of relevant work or study experience abroad; Management in Nonprofit Organisations two years in the non-profit sector plus volunteer work; Development Studies and Governance and Public Policy four months.
funding_summary: The DAAD pays a monthly scholarship of currently EUR 992, exempts holders from tuition fees (a registration fee is still due each semester), and adds a yearly study and research grant of EUR 460, health, accident and liability insurance in Germany, fixed travel lump sums, and rent subsidy and/or family allowances where they apply. A mandatory German course in Germany of up to four months comes before the master's studies. Funding covers the master's course at the chosen university; the courses last two semesters (Development and Governance) or four semesters (the other six).
programmes_note: Scholarships are only for the seven master's courses named in the call, not for any other course in Germany. The courses focus on public policy, good governance, international relations, public management and administration, civil society, social protection, peace and conflict studies, and development and socio-economic policies. You may apply to at most two of them.
institutions_note: Five German universities host the seven courses: University of Applied Sciences Bonn-Rhein-Sieg, University of Duisburg-Essen, University of Erfurt (Willy Brandt School of Public Policy), Otto-von-Guericke University Magdeburg, University of Applied Sciences Osnabrueck and University of Passau (two courses). You send your application to the course or courses you choose, not to the DAAD.

summary.detail: Seven English-taught master's courses at German universities, with studies starting in September or October 2027 after a mandatory German course of up to four months. Six courses last four semesters and one (Development and Governance) lasts two semesters. Social Protection is blended: semester 1 at the university, semester 2 online (in Germany or the home or another developing country), semester 3 a practical term, semester 4 online for the thesis.

benefits.conditions: Partner and children can join for the master's course; the allowance can be requested from the start of studies at the host university (September or October 2027), after the language course. The German embassy alone decides on visas.

requirements.text: Ticked-off checklist and list of criteria, signed by hand with place and date (print, sign, scan and include).
Completed DAAD application form, filled in once with the chosen course or courses. Everything in it must match the letter, CV and any other applications.

One letter of motivation, maximum two pages and dated, giving academic, professional and personal reasons and how they link to the programme's aims. If you apply to two courses, the same letter goes to both and ranks them with reasons.
CV in reverse chronological order in Europass format with the date added; exact details of studies and practical experience; gaps of three months or more explained.

Copies of higher education degree certificates, clearly legible, issued no earlier than 1 January 2020; certified translation if not in German or English. If the certificate is not ready, a confirmation from the university.
Full set of transcripts with an explanation of the grading system, clearly legible; certified translation if not in German or English.

Confirmations of relevant professional experience or internships and/or proof of political activities or community service (volunteering, charities, NGOs), on headed paper with an original or code-certified digital signature, the date and a stamp; certified translation if needed.
Proof of English language skills. The level and certificate differ by course; check with the course.

Current written reference from your current employer, or from a university lecturer only if you are a student at present, on headed paper with an original or code-certified digital signature, the date and a stamp.

application_steps.title: Check eligibility and pick one or two courses
application_steps.detail: Check that you live in a country on the DAAD list, hold an upper-third first degree issued on or after 1 January 2020, have relevant practical experience, and meet the entry rules of the courses. You may apply to a maximum of two of the seven courses; applications to more than two are excluded.

application_steps.title: Prepare the complete document set
application_steps.detail: Read the DAAD selection criteria in the checklist, tick it off and sign it by hand, complete the DAAD application form once, and write one letter of motivation (two pages at most). Add CV, degree certificates, transcripts, proof of practical experience, English proof, reference and, for India and China, an APS certificate. Applications may be in English or German. Only complete sets are considered.

application_steps.title: Send the application to the course, not to the DAAD
application_steps.detail: The application period for all seven courses in this call ran from 1 June to 31 July 2026. Send the form and documents directly to the chosen course or courses (the Willy Brandt School asks for an online application). Applications sent to the DAAD are not forwarded, and any departure from the process leads to exclusion.

application_steps.title: Selection committee meets in October or November 2026
application_steps.detail: A committee of professors from the participating courses and DAAD representatives chooses. The main criteria are a convincing academic, professional and personal motivation linked to the programme's goals, relevant practical experience, and a first degree with upper-third grades. Each course also applies its own criteria.

application_steps.title: Nominated candidates upload full documents to the DAAD portal
application_steps.detail: Candidates proposed for a scholarship are contacted by the DAAD by email and asked to upload their full documents to the DAAD portal. Do not upload anything before being nominated, and keep all documents as PDF copies; send originals only if a course asks.

application_steps.title: Written notice to all applicants
application_steps.detail: All applicants are told in writing after selection ends, expected in December 2026 or January 2027.

application_steps.title: Take the German course in Germany
application_steps.detail: Before the master's course, all holders attend a German course in Germany of up to four months. Participation is mandatory.

application_steps.title: Start the master's course in September or October 2027
application_steps.detail: Studies start in September or October 2027. Holders get support from the programme coordinators at the university, events and seminars for scholarship holders, and networking events. Family members can join; the allowance can be applied for from the start of studies, and the embassy decides on visas. A semester registration fee is payable.

notes: The mandatory German course is described as 'up to four months' in the call and the FAQ, but as 'up to six months' on the DAAD programme page and the course leaflet. The newer call and FAQ (05/2026) are followed in the benefit entry; editors may want to show both.
Duration: the call lists Development and Governance (Duisburg-Essen) as 2 semesters and the others as 4 semesters; the leaflet describes Development and Governance as a one-year programme.

The call text shows the monthly rate as 'currently EUR 992'; stored data for the rate was correct. Stored data on the 15-month residence rule, the 1 January 2020 degree date and the APS certificate was confirmed.

Stored data listed the country codes from the DAAD database page. The country list PDF read now is the OECD DAC list of ODA recipients (reporting on 2025 flows); the stored code list was not re-confirmed against it and is not repeated here.

Dates: the call says the application period for this round was 1 June to 31 July 2026, selection in October/November 2026 and written results in December 2026 or January 2027, so the application period has already ended. The FAQ says the deadline is 31 July each year, with applications opening on 1 June.
